0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Stan:iaids Institution on 30 July 1982, after the draft finalized by the Metallic Finishes Sectional Committee had been approved by the Structural and Metals Division Council. 0.2 This Indian Standard is intended for articles electrodeposited with brass, an alloy deposition of copper and zinc, which is used extensively Brass plating is also applied to steel, being for decorative purposes. effective for strong bonding of rubber to metal. Electroplated brass over aluminium and zinc diecastings, steel tubing and stamping, because of its decorative effect, has been widely used as a substitute for solid brass where weight and cost are factors. Copper conductors have been brass plated as a protection against specific types of corrosion. 0.3 Brass plating as such offers inadequate resistance to corrosion. Due to different conditions of exposure it may not be possible to predict the average life of brass deposit specified in this specification. However, an atterript has been made to obtain satisfactory requirements of brass coating, to form a workable basis between consumers and platers. 0.4 This standard was first published in 1961. It is being revised in sained since its first publication. the light of the experience In this revision ED'I'A methods for the determination of zinc have been incluc!erl. 0.5 For the purpose of tltcitling whether a particular requirement of this stanl`artl is rompl~ed \\.ith, the final value, observed or caltulaled, exprc~ sin? tile ro.ult of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in ac.c ortlance wit11 IS : 2-l!%O*. The number of significant places retained in the: rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

TEST

9.1 Bend Test - Place the sample in a bend tester with 4 mm radius of bending or in a vice as shown in Fig. 2. Bend the sample as far as 90" forward and backward, successive bends being mac!e in opposite direcFor the purpose of this test, one bend shall constitute bending tions. forward to 90" anal back to original position. Repeat this process and count the number of bends until flaking occurs. The sample shall stand three such bends xcithout flaking. 10. COPPER-ZINC RATIO

Neutralize the filtrate with dilute sulphuric acid ( 1:l ) and add 10 ml in Dilute to a sufficient volume with water to cover the gauze of excess. the platinum catho le. Start the stirrer and electrolyae at a current of one ampere until the cathocie is completely covered wirh a deposit of copper; then increase the current to 1.5 A. At the end of 30 minutes, raise the solution level to see if any more copper passes out to the platinum cathode stem. If not; stop the stirring and with the current on, wash the deposit, while lolvering the beaker, receiving the wash water in the beaker. Preserve this solution for the determination of zinc under 10.2 Wash the deposit with water, then with alcohol, dry in an oven at 105�C for about two minutes, cool and weigh. Strip the deposit from the cathode in hot 25 percent nitric acid, wash and dry it as before, then cool and weigh.
